oracle.name: Zotero RIS and BibTeX translator cross-check
oracle.independence: The expected semantics come from Zotero's maintained import/export translators and their checked-in test cases, not from StrumentiUtili.it output.
oracle.selection_policy: Synthetic probes below are minimized from independently maintained Zotero test expectations. They do not copy implementation output and intentionally include cases capable of falsifying this converter.

source_evidence.fact: A1 followed by AU creators are all imported as authors in source order.

ris_to_bibtex.input:
TY  - JOUR
TI  - Mixed creator aliases
A1  - Alpha, Alice
AU  - Beta, Bob
AU  - Gamma, Grace
ER  -

fields.title: Mixed creator aliases
fields.author: Alpha, Alice and Beta, Bob and Gamma, Grace

source_evidence.fact: Y1 is deprecated for the date field and must not override DA when DA is present.

ris_to_bibtex.input:
TY  - JOUR
TI  - Date precedence
DA  - 1950/01/01
Y1  - 1900/01/01
ER  -

source_evidence.fact: For a BOOK record the secondary title represented by T2 is imported as the book series, not a journal title.

ris_to_bibtex.input:
TY  - BOOK
AU  - Writer, Wendy
T1  - Example Book
T2  - Example Series
PY  - 2009
PB  - Example Press
ER  -

source_evidence.fact: RIS date input can carry month/day precision; the converter's declared BibTeX mapping retains only the year.

ris_to_bibtex.input:
TY  - JOUR
TI  - Date precision loss
DA  - 1950/02/03
ER  -

source_evidence.fact: A standard BibTeX article imports as a journal article with title, author, year, journal, volume, issue and pages.

bibtex_to_ris.input: @article{sample, title={Article Title}, volume={107}, number={29}, journal={Example Journal}, author={Oliveira, Ana}, year={2009}, pages={29}}

source_evidence.fact: BibTeX @inbook imports as a book section; the RIS translator exports a book section as TY CHAP.
BibTeX can carry URL-adjacent metadata that has no direct mapping in the converter's declared RIS subset.
